questions.question: A fishing company catching hake off the West Coast belongs to which sector?
A call centre in Cape Town answering customer queries produces no physical good. Its sector is:
options: Primary, because it uses natural airwaves
Tertiary, because it produces a service

questions.question: Which ordering of GDP contribution in South Africa today is correct, largest first?
Agriculture contributes about 3% of GDP yet is still called vital for livelihoods. Why?
options: Because farm prices are controlled by government
Because agriculture pays the highest wages
Because its share of employment, especially rural employment, is larger than its share of GDP

subtopics.title: How the Sectors Link and How the Structure Has Shifted

questions.question: An orange grown in Limpopo, juiced in Nelspruit and sold by a supermarket passes through the sectors in which order?
The historical pattern in which an economy's weight moves from primary to secondary to tertiary is called:
South Africa's manufacturing share of GDP since the early 1990s has:
Why is premature deindustrialisation a particular worry for South Africa?
options: Manufacturing historically absorbs semi-skilled workers in large numbers, which a high-unemployment economy needs
Factories pay more tax than banks

questions.question: Which item is SOCIAL rather than economic infrastructure?
How does a clinic contribute to production, according to the lesson?
options: Indirectly — healthier workers are more productive
It does not; social infrastructure is pure consumption

questions.question: Load shedding and freight-rail failures are described as acting like a tax because they:
options: Raise costs for producers in all three sectors at the same time

questions.question: Coal exporters recently lost sales mainly because:
options: South Africa's coal reserves ran out
Rail and port bottlenecks meant volumes could not be moved
World demand for coal fell to zero

subtopics.title: Service Provisioning, Access and Economic Opportunity

questions.question: Roughly what share of South African households is connected to electricity?
Where is access to services weakest, according to the lesson?
options: Rural former homeland areas and informal settlements

questions.question: The 'digital divide' in South Africa mainly refers to:
options: Different TV channels in different provinces
The gap between Android and iPhone users
Poorer households paying relatively more, via mobile data, to get online — or staying offline

questions.question: The lesson's core mechanism linking services to opportunity is that poor access:
options: Raises the cost of participating in the economy, most heavily for the poor

subtopics.title: From the Ground, Through the Factory, Over the Counter

questions.question: The mill that grinds mealies into maize meal belongs to which sector?
Out of every R100 South Africa produces, services contribute roughly:
The lesson's one-line correction of a common belief is that South Africa is:
options: A farming economy with a few banks
A mining economy with a few shops
A factory economy with no mines
A services economy with famous mines

subtopics.title: One Street, All Three Sectors Holding Hands

questions.question: If the wheat harvest fails, the vetkoek seller eventually suffers because:
options: Trouble in one sector travels down the chain to the others

questions.question: Which era ordering matches South Africa's economic history?
options: Services years, factory years, mines-and-farms years
Factory years, services years, mines-and-farms years
Mines-and-farms years, factory years, services years

questions.question: Factory jobs are described as especially valuable for South Africa because they:
options: Suit workers with skills and willingness but without university degrees
Are the highest paid in the world

subtopics.title: The Wires and Pipes That Decide Who Gets to Play

questions.question: During the load-shedding day at the chicken shop, output fell because:
options: A shared infrastructure failure stopped fryers, fridges and card machines at once

questions.question: Why do economists call fixing power, rail and ports the cheapest way to grow?
options: Because repairing one shared thing lowers costs for every producer at once
Because it replaces the need for education

questions.question: A job 20 km away can be worthless to a poor worker because:
options: Taxi fares can consume so much of the wage that the job no longer pays
Jobs may not legally be advertised that far away

questions.question: The lesson's final mechanism is: unequal access to services leads to:
